commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Order the compact mesh as data, expert, context (#10877)

Order the compact Grug mesh as `(replica_dcn, data, expert, context,
model)`. The old order was `(replica_dcn, data, context, expert,
model)`. This is an alternative to #10709.

- The hero's dropless eval folds `expert` into `data`. With `data` next
to `expert`, the eval mesh is a reshape of the training mesh. Each
device keeps its training context group. Its eval data group is its
training `(data, expert)` group.
- Under the old order, at CP > 1 the reshape made device groups that
training does not use. XLA keeps an NCCL communicator for each new group
outside the allocator pool. At 65K CP4 this used 7.4 GiB per GPU and
crashed the eval.
- The new order makes the device transpose and spec rename from #10709
unnecessary. #10711 can remove its copy of that code.
- On 16 CPU devices, the compiled eval uses only device groups that the
training step also uses. The old order adds 10 groups at data 1 × expert
8 × context 2.
- At CP1 no device moves, so the 65K hero does not change.
- At CP > 1 the physical layout changes: at CP4 × EP16, each 4-GPU tray
holds one context group. CP > 1 PGLE profiles need new measurements.
- A 12-node GB200 A/B at 262K, CP4 × EP12, 288 experts, random init and
45 steps found no regression. The median step time was 22.91 s with this
change and 22.88 s on main (+0.4%), against a step-to-step spread of
about 2 s. Peak memory was 132.2 and 132.3 GiB. The dropless eval
completed in 123 s and 125 s. Main did not hit the communicator OOM at
this size, so this run does not test the eval fix. A full-rack CP4 ×
EP16 run from a hero checkpoint has not run.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[taskforge] Deliver image-job credentials as Iris secrets (#10866)

Image jobs now read a failed build's exit code from its task. The
controller's `GetJobStatus` sets only aggregate counts: `tasks` is empty
and the job-level `exit_code` is 0. `wait_succeeded` therefore asks
`job.task(0).status()`, which matches the one-task, no-retry image jobs.
Before, a crane or kaniko-export bootstrap failure (exit 125) was raised
as `BuildFailed`, a Dockerfile error, instead of the host's
`ImageJobFailed`.

The registry credential and the CoreWeave storage keys now reach the
image jobs as Iris secrets (`EnvironmentSpec.secrets`, still under
`SecretBehavior.ISOLATE`), and `image_push` reads them from files under
`$RIGGING_SECRETS_DIR`. They no longer appear in either job's
environment or pod spec. A coordinator job receives the registry
credential as the Iris secret `TASKFORGE_REGISTRY_CREDENTIAL` and reads
it with `require_secret`. Laptops still read it with `gcloud`, because
rigging's `gcp-secret://` resolver needs `google-cloud-secret-manager`,
which taskforge does not declare. Inherited environment values are still
blanked, except a parent's explicit `CW_KEY_ID`/`CW_KEY_SECRET`: Iris
lets those override the secrets of the same name, so blanking them would
leave the jobs with empty storage keys. The build job still carries the
submitter's CoreWeave key, which Iris requires on every CoreWeave job
and the output uploader uses. No key scoped to the output-archive prefix
exists yet, and the module docstring records the exposure.

A live build-to-pull run on `cw-us-east-02a` at 1a2b95385a, submitted
from a laptop, built, pushed and read back a linux/amd64 image by digest
in 83 s
([record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10293#discussion_r4455935215)).
It covers the exit-code and secret-file changes. It did not start a
container from the image.

The container backend now comes from the selected factories rather than
a host enum. `container_backend(backends)` returns the single `GVISOR`
or `DOCKER` entry and raises if there is none or more than one, so
`lower`, `machine_runtime` and `machine_backend` take the factories and
`MachineHost` is removed.

`task_refusals` and its refusal types are deleted, since
`spec.draft.lower` already runs `RolloutEngine.check` on the same
factories. `warm_local_python` and `PythonEnvironmentFactory` are
deleted because nothing in the repository calls them.
`scripts/build_image_job.py` uses click. `publish_with_timings` is
synchronous and only `ImageBuilder.publish` stays async, because #10298
awaits it inside an `asyncio.TaskGroup`.

The stacked #10298, #10300 and #10301 need to follow. `lower` loses its
`host` argument, so `BuildServiceConfig.host`,
`infrastructure.host_backends` and `host_checked_factories` should take
the backends. `round._lower` and `trials.run_trial` lose
`task_refusals`, and `build_process` should read the registry credential
with `rigging.secrets.get_secret`.

Follow-up to #10293.

Serialize tokenizer staging across local processes (#10797)

Serialize tokenizer staging across local processes with a file lock
beside the shared staging directory. Waiting callers recheck the
completed local files under the lock and reuse them, preventing another
download from truncating files during loading.

A subprocess regression holds one filesystem copy halfway through while
a second loader starts. The baseline leaves zero-filled bytes in
tokenizer.json and fails to load; with the lock, both processes load the
complete tokenizer. The same file lock coordinates both threads and
processes.

The affected CPU suite passed 1,670 tests with seven skipped. Its five
checkpoint-path failures also reproduce on unchanged main.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[merging] Allow BF16 and FP16 merge source widening (#10597)

Allow merge sources to widen allowlisted BF16 or FP16 tensors to FP32
when loading shards. The
`marianna13/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-SFT-mix-v4-think-step465`
checkpoint stores 26 `model.layers.N.mlp.router.bias` tensors as BF16.
The other merge parents store those tensors as FP32, so `merge_tensor`
rejects the mismatch.

`CheckpointSource.dtype_widenings` maps full-match tensor-key regexes to
a declared stored and loaded dtype pair. Only `bfloat16 -> float32` and
`float16 -> float32` are allowed. A matched tensor with a different
stored dtype raises; unmatched tensors retain their dtype. Merge
arithmetic remains FP32 and output uses the anchor dtype. The policy
appears in the recipe and manifest; input shards are unchanged.

For the SFT-465 source, add:

```json
{
  "dtype_widenings": {
    "model\\.layers\\.(?:[0-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-5])\\.mlp\\.router\\.bias": ["bfloat16", "float32"]
  }
}
```

Synthetic shard tests cover both promotions and mismatched stored
dtypes. `uv run --no-project infra/ci/run_tests.py` passed all 70
selected safe tests.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Add a daily one-rack hero canary on GB200 (#10861)

Add a daily canary that runs the hero model and training step from main
on one GB200 NVL72 rack, so throughput regressions show up before a hero
deploy. It uses `launch_diagnostics` with the hero's defaults, restores
the pinned permanent checkpoint `step-372000`, trains 35 updates on the
production mixture and runs one dropless eval after the last update.
Every run sees the same weights and batches, so a step-time change comes
from the code. Settings that only the production launcher applies, such
as `gate_router_weight_decay` and `prior_context_phases`, are left out;
they do not change step time.

The workflow submits at 11:00 UTC (3 AM PST, 6 AM EST) at `batch`
priority, the band of the hero-completions sampler, so neither preempts
the other. It waits up to five hours for the training job to start, then
for the run, and scores it against the per-metric median of the last
five scheduled runs from the same checkpoint. Manual dispatches are
named `hero-canary-manual-*` and never enter that baseline. A step-time
change beyond 1.5% posts its own Slack message, since the run stays
green. If no rack frees up in time, `iris_monitor.py wait` cancels the
job under the new `--child-wait-timeout-policy shutdown` and the day is
skipped with a notice; a failed run alerts through Slack and Loom. The
default policy still fails on timeout, so other canaries are unchanged.
A healthy run holds the rack for about 20 minutes.

Scored against Matt's one-rack 65K test (`tok350-deploy65k-c1-01`), the
report gives 15.572 s/step, 34.41% MFU and 127.9 GiB peak HBM, matching
#10820. Over 30 steady steps the median step time is within about ±0.5%,
so the report flags changes beyond 1.5%. That threshold is provisional
until two same-commit runs measure run-to-run variance.

Over the last two months the GB200 fleet had a median of 8 idle nodes. A
five-hour window from 11:00 UTC contained a 30-minute stretch with 16 or
more idle nodes on 22 of 62 days, so most days will be skipped until the
queue behavior is known from real runs. One rack does not exercise
cross-rack collectives or checkpoint recovery. The Loom triage binding
needs a `pulumi up` of `infra/loom` after merge, and the first run can
only start once the workflow is on main.

The MFU tracker lane is Open-Athena/mfu-tracker#15.

[levanter] Preserve integral mixture allocations after normalization (#10793)

Preserve exact integer mixture allocations after normalizing weights.
Floating-point roundoff can turn `1001 / 64000 * 64000` into a value
just below 1001; truncation then silently moves one document to the
largest component. Snap values within 1e-9 of an integer before the
existing remainder allocation.

All 23 mixture tests pass, including the normalized-count regression.
The affected suite passed 1,591 tests with seven skips; its five
checkpoint-path failures reproduce unchanged on main `671c7bcf78`.
Mechanical checks and independent library/advisory reviews passed.

commits.message:
Replace CPU test scripts with multi-device tests (#10713)

Replace embedded CPU test scripts with ordinary Python tests so imports,
dependencies, and assertions remain visible to source analysis. JAX
backend resets provide the requested CPU device count locally; tests use
native TPU or GPU devices when available.

`multidevice` marks multi-device tests that also work on CPU. CPU CI
runs them with the required CPU device count. The Levanter TPU lane runs
its marked multi-device tests when the hardware has enough devices;
tests whose topology requires eight devices remain CPU-only on the
current four-device TPU runner. Root and experiment tests stay in their
existing CI scopes.
